cards.questionEn: Why must an aircraft take off within the applicable holdover time after ground de-icing or anti-icing?
cards.questionZh: 飞机在地面除冰或防冰后，为什么必须在适用的保持时间内起飞？
cards.answerEn: Anti-icing fluid loses effectiveness over time. If takeoff is delayed beyond the applicable holdover time, ice, snow, or frost may accumulate again on critical surfaces. This contamination can reduce lift and increase drag, so the aircraft must be treated again before takeoff.

selectedSources.sourceQuestionEn: What is holding time? Why is it important for de-icing and anti-icing?
selectedSources.text: Holding time is the estimated period during which an anti-icing fluid will protect the aircraft from ice, snow, or frost accumulation. It starts when the final anti-icing application begins and ends when the fluid loses effectiveness. Holding time depends on the fluid type, weather conditions, and precipitation intensity. It is important because if takeoff exceeds the holding time, the aircraft may have new ice contamination on critical surfaces like wings. This reduces lift and increases drag. Pilots must check the holding time on the de-icing certificate. If takeoff is delayed beyond this time, the aircraft must return for re-treatment. Safety depends on respecting holding time.

selectedSources.sourceQuestionEn: What happens if a pilot exceeds the holding time after applying anti-icing fluid?
selectedSources.text: If the holding time is exceeded, the anti-icing fluid loses its effectiveness. Ice, snow, or frost may start to accumulate again on the aircraft surfaces, especially on the wings and tail. Contamination on critical surfaces reduces lift, increases drag, and may cause early stall or loss of control. Therefore, the pilot must not take off after exceeding holding time. Instead, the aircraft must return to the de-icing pad for re-treatment. The pilot should inform ATC and ground handling of the delay. During taxi, if snow or freezing rain continues, the pilot may need to request a shorter holding time estimate. Never take off if you are uncertain about the condition of the wings after holding time has expired.

cards.questionEn: What is the difference between de-icing and anti-icing?
cards.questionZh: 除冰与防冰有什么区别？
cards.answerEn: De-icing removes ice, snow, or frost that has already accumulated on an aircraft. Anti-icing helps prevent new ice from forming after de-icing. Many operations use de-icing first and anti-icing second.

selectedSources.sourceQuestionEn: What is the difference between de-icing and anti-icing?
selectedSources.text: De-icing removes ice, snow, or frost that has already accumulated on the aircraft surfaces. Anti-icing prevents new ice from forming after de-icing. De-icing is usually done using hot fluid under pressure. Anti-icing uses a thicker fluid that sticks to the surface and absorbs moisture. In practice, most operations use a two-step process: first de-icing to clean the aircraft, then anti-icing to protect it before takeoff. Some fluids combine both functions. Pilots must understand the difference because the holding time starts after the final anti-icing application. Using only de-icing without anti-icing in active precipitation is dangerous.

editActions: extracted the core distinction
removed operational details not needed for the comparison

cards.questionEn: What is holdover time in ground de-icing and anti-icing operations?
cards.questionZh: 在地面除冰和防冰作业中，什么是保持时间？
cards.answerEn: Holdover time is the estimated period during which anti-icing fluid protects an aircraft from ice, snow, or frost accumulation. It begins when the final anti-icing application starts and ends when the fluid loses effectiveness. It depends on the fluid type, weather, and precipitation intensity; if it expires before takeoff, new contamination may form and re-treatment may be needed.

selectedSources.sourceQuestionEn: What is holding time? Why is it important for de-icing and anti-icing?
selectedSources.text: Holding time is the estimated period during which an anti-icing fluid will protect the aircraft from ice, snow, or frost accumulation. It starts when the final anti-icing application begins and ends when the fluid loses effectiveness. Holding time depends on the fluid type, weather conditions, and precipitation intensity. It is important because if takeoff exceeds the holding time, the aircraft may have new ice contamination on critical surfaces like wings. This reduces lift and increases drag. Pilots must check the holding time on the de-icing certificate. If takeoff is delayed beyond this time, the aircraft must return for re-treatment. Safety depends on respecting holding time.

selectedSources.text: There are four main fluid types based on SAE standards. Type I is orange and used for de-icing. It is thin, heated, and runs off quickly. It provides very short holding time. Type IV is green and the most common anti-icing fluid for large jets. It is very thick and provides the longest holding time. Type I is for de-icing only. Types II and IV are for anti-icing. selectedSources.sourceQuestionEn: Who is responsible for deciding whether de-icing or anti-icing is needed before takeoff?
selectedSources.text: The pilot in command has the final responsibility for deciding whether de-icing or anti-icing is required. Before takeoff, the captain must check the outside air temperature, visibility, and precipitation. If there is frost, ice, or snow on the wings or control surfaces, de-icing is mandatory. The pilot cannot rely solely on ground crew recommendations. However, the pilot should consult with the airline’s dispatch and ground de-icing personnel for technical advice. Ultimately, if the captain has any doubt about ice contamination, they should request de-icing. Taking off with ice on critical surfaces is illegal and extremely dangerous. The final go/no-go decision belongs to the captain.

selectedSources.sourceQuestionEn: What type of de-icing or anti-icing fluid should be used in heavy snow conditions?
selectedSources.text: In heavy snow conditions, a two-step process is recommended. First, use heated Type I fluid for de-icing to remove existing snow and ice. Then apply Type IV anti-icing fluid, which provides the longest holding time under severe weather. Type IV is very thick and can withstand heavy snow for a limited period. However, even Type IV has a maximum holding time. If snow accumulation is extreme, the pilot may need to request repeated de-icing just before takeoff. Some operators use Type II as an alternative, but Type IV is preferred for heavy snow. Never use only Type I in active heavy snow because it offers almost no holding time. Always check the fluid’s certified weather conditions.

cards.taskTitle: 运行-复杂/特殊机场运行-1
cards.questionEn: What factors can cause an aircraft to overrun the runway after landing?
cards.questionZh: 哪些因素可能导致航空器着陆后冲出跑道？
cards.answerEn: A runway overrun can result from an unstable or high approach, a tailwind, poor braking action on a wet, icy, or snowy runway, or landing without the normal flap configuration. Brake or thrust-reverser problems, a short runway, or exceeding aircraft performance limits can also contribute.

selectedSources.sourceQuestionEn: What factors may cause the aircraft to overrun the runway after landing?
selectedSources.text:
There are many factors that may cause the aircraft to overrun the runway after landing.
First, if the flaps are jammed during approach, the landing speed is higher than normal, the aircraft may overrun the runway.
Second, if the aircraft is above the glide slope during landing, the aircraft may overshoot the runway.
Third, if there are problems with brakes or thrust reversers, it may cause the aircraft to run out of runway.

selectedSources.sourceQuestionEn: What factors may cause the aircraft to overrun the runway after landing?
selectedSources.text: Key factors include poor braking action (runway water/icing/snow), unstable approach, flapless landing, tailwind, pilot's inadequate skills, gear-up/belly landing, and exceeding aircraft performance limits.

selectedSources.sourceQuestionEn: What factors may cause the aircraft overrun the runway after landing?
selectedSources.text: There are some reasons for aircraft overrun the runway after landing. For example, overshooting during approach, brakes or thrust reverser malfunction, landing in tailwind, landing on short and narrow runway.

removed questionable skill attribution
cards.riskAssessment: Every factor is explicit in v1.

cards.taskTitle: 运行-复杂/特殊机场运行-3
cards.questionEn: How can pilots safely take off from and land on short and narrow runways?
cards.questionZh: 飞行员如何在短而窄的跑道上安全起飞和着陆？
cards.answerEn: Pilots should assess the weather, runway condition, and aircraft performance before flight and follow the applicable SOP. They should use the full available runway, maintain directional control during takeoff, and determine the required landing distance before landing. They should conduct an approach briefing, confirm how duties will be shared, and be prepared to reject the takeoff, go around, or divert if needed.

selectedSources.sourceQuestionEn: What should a pilot do to ensure the flight safety in taking off or land on short and narrow runways?
selectedSources.text: There are many things we should do when taking off on short and narrow runways. First, we should make preflight preparation to get the weather conditions about the airport and the performance of the aircraft. Second, we should follow standard operation procedures, especially in case of strong wind, low visibility and runway contamination. Third, we should use full length runway for departure and keep the directional control of the aircraft.

selectedSources.sourceQuestionEn: What should a pilot do to ensure the flight safety in taking off or land on short and narrow runways?
selectedSources.text: There are many things we should do when landing on short and narrow runways First, we should follow the checklist to determine the required landing distance. If there is contamination on the runway or mechanical problems such as flaps jammed and the landing distance can’t meet the requirement, we should divert or return to land. Second, we should make the approach briefing and confirm the task-sharing. Third we should use precision approach, such as ILS approach and land into windFourth, we should avoid overshooting.

selectedSources.sourceQuestionEn: What should a pilot do to ensure the flight safety in taking off or land on short and narrow runways?
selectedSources.text: Pilots should strictly control speed, ensure sufficient thrust, maintain stable attitude, follow SOP, conduct preflight performance assessment, request the longest available runway, and be prepared for go-around or takeoff rejection if needed.

limited distance calculation to landing and removed the rigid approach-method claim

cards.questionEn: What are the limitations of weather radar?
cards.questionZh: 气象雷达有哪些局限性？
cards.answerEn: Weather radar detects precipitation, so it does not show dry turbulence, clear-air turbulence, or volcanic ash directly. Heavy rain can attenuate the signal, and a strong return can hide weather behind it through radar shadowing. An incorrect tilt setting may also show ground returns instead of the weather of interest. Pilots should therefore use other weather information and visual observation as well.

selectedSources.sourceQuestionEn: What are the limitations of weather radar?
selectedSources.text: Weather radar has several limitations. First, it only detects precipitation, not turbulence directly. Turbulence is inferred from precipitation intensity. Second, radar shadowing occurs when a strong storm blocks the radar beam, hiding weather behind it. Third, attenuation happens in heavy rain, reducing the radar's ability to see beyond the storm. Fourth, the radar cannot detect dry turbulence, clear air turbulence, or volcanic ash. Fifth, the tilt setting must be adjusted correctly; if set too low, it may show ground returns instead of weather. Finally, storms can develop faster than the radar can update. Therefore, pilots should never rely solely on weather radar. They should also use ATC weather reports, onboard lightning sensors, and visual observation. Safety requires multiple sources of information.

cards.questionEn: What is the function of the Ground Proximity Warning System (GPWS)?
cards.questionZh: 近地警告系统（GPWS）有什么功能？
cards.answerEn: The function of GPWS is to help prevent controlled flight into terrain. It monitors the aircraft’s proximity to the ground and gives the flight crew aural and visual warnings when there is a terrain-collision risk.

selectedSources.sourceQuestionEn:
What is the function of GPWS?

selectedSources.text: The Ground Proximity Warning System (GPWS) is designed to prevent CFIT (controlled flight into terrain). It can give flight crew some advanced warning, both aurally and visually, if the aircraft is too close to the ground.

selectedSources.sourceQuestionEn:

selectedSources.text: GPWS stands for Ground Proximity Warning System. It uses radio altimeter and flight computers to monitor the aircraft’s distance to terrain. When the aircraft is at risk of collision, it issues aural (for example “pull up”) and visual warnings, helping pilots avoid CFIT (Controlled Flight into Terrain) accidents.

cards.questionEn: How does the Ground Proximity Warning System (GPWS) work?
cards.questionZh: 近地警告系统（GPWS）如何工作？
cards.answerEn: GPWS uses radio-altimeter information to monitor the aircraft’s height above the ground. Its different operating modes compare that height with conditions such as the aircraft’s descent rate. If the aircraft is too close to the ground or descending too rapidly near it, the system gives a warning such as “Sink rate.”

cards.questionEn: What should the remaining pilot do if the other pilot becomes incapacitated during flight?
cards.questionZh: 飞行中一名飞行员失能时，另一名飞行员应如何处置？
cards.answerEn: The remaining pilot should take control and stabilize the aircraft, using the autopilot if conditions allow. The cabin crew should be asked to assess the incapacitated pilot and provide first aid, while the remaining crew redistribute essential duties. The pilot should inform ATC and prepare to land at a suitable airport, requesting medical assistance when needed.

Third, I will report the situation to ATC and request divert to the nearest suitable airport and medical assistance upon arrival.

Then, I’ll assess the first officer’s condition and try to provide necessary aid. After that, I’ll inform ATC about the situation, following emergency procedures, and prepare for a possible solo - handled approach and landing, making sure to prioritize flight safety and passenger welfare throughout the process.

cards.taskTitle: 其它-航空发展与新技术-1
cards.questionEn: How do you think China's aviation industry will develop over the next ten years?
cards.questionZh: 你认为未来十年中国航空业将如何发展？
cards.answerEn: I think China’s aviation industry will continue to grow over the next ten years. Airlines may expand their fleets and route networks, use more domestically produced aircraft, and apply technologies such as artificial intelligence and big data in operations and passenger services. The industry is also likely to focus more on cleaner aircraft and fuels and on training pilots, controllers, and maintenance personnel.

selectedSources.sourceQuestionEn: What do you think the aviation industry in China will be like in 10 years from now?
selectedSources.text: I am very optimistic about the development of China's civil aviation in the next decade. Firstly, in terms of fleet expansion, with the continuous growth of market demand and the maturity of domestic aircraft such as the C919, Chinese airlines will continue to expand their fleets, increasing the proportion of domestic aircraft and reducing dependence on foreign aircraft. Secondly, in terms of route network expansion, China's civil aviation will further improve the domestic route network, strengthen the connection between large and medium-sized cities and small and medium-sized cities, and at the same time expand international routes, enhancing China's status as an international aviation hub. Thirdly, in terms of technological innovation, China's civil aviation will continue to promote the application of new technologies such as artificial intelligence, big data and the Internet of Things in flight operations, air traffic control and passenger services, improving operational efficiency and safety levels. In addition, in terms of green development, affected by the global call for environmental protection, China's civil aviation will pay more attention to energy conservation and emission reduction, promote the use of more environmentally friendly aircraft and fuels, and achieve sustainable development. selectedSources.sourceQuestionEn: What do you know about SAF?

SAF stands for Sustainable Aviation Fuel. It is a type of aviation fuel made from renewable sources such as used cooking oil, agricultural waste, animal fats, or even household garbage. Unlike traditional jet fuel which comes from crude oil, SAF reduces carbon dioxide emissions by up to 80% over its lifecycle. SAF can be blended with conventional jet fuel and used in existing aircraft engines without modification. Currently, most aircraft can operate with a blend of up to 50% SAF. Airlines are increasingly using SAF to reduce environmental impact and meet international climate goals. The main challenges are limited supply and higher cost.

cards.answerEn: The grooves drain water away from the runway surface and make it harder for a continuous water film to form beneath the tyres. cards.answerEn: The airport should inspect the grooves regularly for wear, blockage, damaged edges, and cracks. It should also check that their depth and width meet the applicable requirements. cards.questionEn: What should a pilot do if radio communication becomes intermittent or unreliable?

cards.questionEn: Do you think an effective briefing with the cabin crew can improve the chances of a successful emergency evacuation? Why?

cards.answerEn: Yes. An effective briefing makes each crew member's responsibilities clear and improves teamwork between the flight crew and cabin crew. During an evacuation, that clarity helps the pilots complete their checklist while the cabin crew prepares and guides the passengers, making the process more orderly and efficient.

cards.questionEn: What procedures should a flight crew follow when conducting an emergency evacuation?
cards.questionZh: 进行紧急撤离时，机组应遵循哪些程序？
cards.answerEn: The crew should stop and secure the aircraft, shut down the engines and power as required, and complete the evacuation checklist. They should advise ATC, request emergency assistance, and coordinate with the cabin crew. The cabin crew should use safe exits, deploy slides when appropriate, direct passengers to leave their baggage, and move everyone away from the aircraft after evacuation.

Fourth, the cabin crew will open the emergency exits and emergency slides and lead the passengers to leave the aircraft in time and in order. We will be the last one to leave the aircraft.

selectedSources.sourceQuestionEn: What are the procedures of executing emergency evacuation?
selectedSources.text: Stop the aircraft, set parking brakes, cut off engines and power. Inform cabin crew to prepare evacuation, report to ATC and request fire/medical assistance. Instruct passengers to brace for impact, open emergency exits, and guide orderly evacuation.

selectedSources.sourceQuestionEn: What about emergency evacuation on the runway? Can you explain the standard procedures?
selectedSources.text: After stopping safely on the runway, the captain immediately orders emergency evacuation. The crew activates emergency lights and briefs passengers to leave baggage behind. Pilots shut down engines, fuel, and electric systems. Flight attendants open exits and deploy slides if safe. Passengers evacuate quickly and move away from the aircraft. Pilots are the last to leave, checking the cockpit and cabin. After evacuation, the crew gathers passengers at a safe distance and reports to rescue services. Evacuation must be completed within 90 seconds. The captain coordinates with ATC and emergency services throughout. Safety is the top priority.

cards.questionEn: What can cause in-flight depressurization?
cards.questionZh: 哪些因素可能导致飞行中失压？
cards.answerEn: In-flight depressurization can result from a pressurization-system failure, an outflow-valve malfunction, an air-conditioning pack problem, or a bleed-air leak. It can also be caused by an improperly sealed door or by structural damage to a door, window, windshield, or the aircraft skin.

cards.questionEn: How do slow and rapid depressurization differ in the risks they present?
cards.questionZh: 缓慢失压和快速失压所带来的风险有何不同？
cards.answerEn: Rapid depressurization causes a sudden loss of pressure and oxygen, so the crew and passengers may become incapacitated before they can respond. Slow depressurization is less obvious because hypoxia develops gradually, making the problem difficult to detect. Both are dangerous, but they present different warning and response challenges.

selectedSources.sourceQuestionEn: In your opinion, which situation is more dangerous in flight, slow depressurization or rapid depressurization?
selectedSources.text: Both are dangerous, but rapid decompression is more critical. It causes sudden oxygen and pressure loss, leading to crew/passenger incapacitation in seconds before oxygen masks are donned, especially at cruising altitude. Slow decompression is insidious, as hypoxia develops gradually, making it hard to detect early, which may also lead to loss of control.

cards.taskTitle: 飞机系统-电力系统失效-4
cards.questionEn: When is external electrical power used on an aircraft?
cards.questionZh: 航空器在什么时候使用外部电源？
cards.answerEn: External electrical power is used while the aircraft is on the ground, normally before the engines are started. It is particularly useful when the APU is unavailable.

selectedSources.sourceQuestionEn: When do pilots need to use external power?
selectedSources.text: Sometimes, when we are on the ground, we will use external power.

selectedSources.sourceQuestionEn: When do pilots need to use external power?
selectedSources.text: When we are on the ground, before engines are started and APU is inoperative (INOP), we will use external power.

editActions: combined the ground, pre-start, and APU-unavailable conditions
repaired grammar
cards.riskAssessment: Both operating conditions are explicit in v1.

cards.taskTitle: 飞机系统-电力系统失效-5
cards.questionEn: When might the APU be used to supply electrical power?
cards.questionZh: 在什么情况下可以使用 APU 供电？
cards.answerEn: On the ground, the APU may supply electrical power before the engines are started, especially when a ground power unit is unavailable. In flight, it may provide power after an engine failure if the APU is available for that operation.

selectedSources.sourceQuestionEn: When do pilots need to use APU for power supply?
selectedSources.text: When we are on the ground or there is an engine failure during flight, we will use the APU for power supply.

selectedSources.sourceQuestionEn: When do pilots need to use APU for power supply?
selectedSources.text: When we are on the ground, before engines are started and GPU is not available, we will use APU for power supply. When we are in the air, if the engines fail, we will use APU for power supply.

editActions: kept ground use before engine start and possible in-flight emergency use
made in-flight availability conditional
cards.riskAssessment: Both uses are explicit in v1; conditional wording avoids treating in-flight APU use as universal.

cards.taskTitle: 飞机系统-电力系统失效-6
cards.questionEn: What are the main functions of an aircraft's electrical system?
cards.questionZh: 航空器电气系统的主要功能有哪些？
cards.answerEn: The electrical system supplies power to essential aircraft systems and flight instruments. It supports lighting, navigation, communication, instrument displays, flight controls, air conditioning, passenger services, and emergency equipment.

selectedSources.sourceQuestionEn: What are the functions of electrical system?
selectedSources.text: The electrical system is used to provide electrical power to essential systems, flight instruments and passenger services.

selectedSources.sourceQuestionEn: What are the functions of electrical system?
selectedSources.text: Electrical systems supply power to aircraft components, including lights, navigation equipment, instrument displays, communication systems, flight control systems, air conditioning, and emergency equipment. They are essential for normal flight operation and emergency response.

editActions: grouped essential, operational, passenger, and emergency loads
removed repetitive wording
cards.riskAssessment: Every function is explicit in v1.

cards.taskTitle: 飞机系统-电力系统失效-7
cards.questionEn: What should a flight crew do if an electrical system failure occurs during flight?
cards.questionZh: 飞行中电气系统失效时，飞行机组应怎么做？
cards.answerEn: The crew should use any available standby instruments to maintain control and navigation. They should inform ATC, declare an emergency if necessary, and divert to a suitable airport.

selectedSources.sourceQuestionEn: If you encounter electrical failure during flight, what will you do?
selectedSources.text: First, we will report our situation to ATC and request radar vectors to the nearest suitable airport. Second, we will identify the faulty circuit and shut off non - essential electrical loads. Third, we will land as soon as possible.

selectedSources.sourceQuestionEn: If you encounter electrical failure during flight, what will you do?
selectedSources.text: Switch to backup power (battery or RAT) immediately. Use standby analog instruments for navigation and control. Isolate the faulty electrical system to prevent further damage. Report to ATC, declare emergency if necessary, and request diversion to the nearest airport. Minimize non-essential electrical loads to conserve power.

editActions: kept available standby instruments, ATC notification, conditional emergency declaration, and diversion
removed universal electrical reconfiguration, radar-vector, and immediate-landing wording
cards.riskAssessment: Every retained response is explicit in v1; non-universal electrical reconfiguration, navigation, and landing instructions were excluded.

cards.taskTitle: 飞机系统-电力系统失效-8
cards.questionEn: What can cause an aircraft electrical system to fail during flight?
cards.questionZh: 哪些因素可能导致航空器电气系统在飞行中失效？
cards.answerEn: An electrical failure may be caused by a generator or alternator failure, a short circuit, damaged wiring, overheating, or a battery malfunction. Lightning, an onboard fire, or improper maintenance can also lead to a failure.

selectedSources.sourceQuestionEn: What reasons may cause electrical system to fail during flight?
selectedSources.text: There are many reasons for electrical failure. First, engine/generator failure may cause electrical failure. Second, lightning strike may cause failure. Third, fire on board may cause electrical failure. Besides, there are some other reasons for electrical failure.

selectedSources.sourceQuestionEn: What reasons may cause electrical system to fail during flight?
selectedSources.text: Key causes include lightning strike, electrical short circuit, overheating, generator/alternator failure, improper maintenance, wiring damage, or battery malfunction. Severe weather (e.g., turbulence) or bird strike may also indirectly trigger electrical system failures.

editActions: kept direct electrical, component, maintenance, weather, and fire causes
removed speculative bird-strike and turbulence claims
cards.riskAssessment: Every retained cause is explicit in v1; speculative indirect causes were excluded.

cards.taskTitle: 飞机系统-电力系统失效-9
cards.questionEn: How can an electrical system failure affect an aircraft and its operation?
cards.questionZh: 电气系统失效会如何影响航空器及其运行？
cards.answerEn: An electrical failure can cause the loss of instrument displays, lighting, navigation, or communication equipment. It may disconnect the autopilot and increase the crew's workload. It can also be associated with smoke or an onboard fire.

selectedSources.sourceQuestionEn: What kind of problems may be caused by electrical system failure?
selectedSources.text: If there is electrical system failure, first, it may cause digital flight instrument failure. Second, it may cause loss of communication and navigation. Third, it may cause fire on board.

selectedSources.sourceQuestionEn: What kind of problems may be caused by electrical system failure?
selectedSources.text: Electrical failure can lead to loss of instrument displays, navigation/communication systems malfunction, lighting failure, autopilot disconnection, and in-flight fire or smoke. It may also affect hydraulic, pressurization, and fuel systems, reducing aircraft controllability and endangering flight safety.

editActions: kept direct display, navigation, communication, lighting, autopilot, smoke, and fire effects
removed broad secondary-system claims
cards.riskAssessment: Every retained operational effect is explicit in v1.

cards.taskTitle: 飞机系统-电力系统失效-10
cards.questionEn: What should a flight crew do if an electrical failure causes the loss of cockpit displays?
cards.questionZh: 电气故障导致驾驶舱显示器失效时，飞行机组应怎么做？
cards.answerEn: The crew should use backup power and the standby instruments to maintain control and navigation. They can request radar vectors from ATC if that service is available. If necessary, they should declare urgency and divert to a suitable airport.

selectedSources.sourceQuestionEn: If you encounter navaids display failure because of electrical power, what are you going to do？
selectedSources.text: If there is navigation display malfunction, we will use standby instruments and request radar vectors.

selectedSources.sourceQuestionEn: If you encounter display failure because of electrical power, what are you going to do?
selectedSources.text: Switch to backup power and use standby analog instruments (e.g., attitude indicator, altimeter) for flight control. Request radar vectors from ATC for navigation. Isolate the faulty electrical bus to prevent system spread. Declare urgency if needed and divert to the nearest suitable airport for maintenance.

editActions: kept backup power, standby instruments, ATC navigation support, urgency, and diversion
removed the universal electrical-bus isolation instruction
cards.riskAssessment: Every retained response is explicit in v1; availability wording limits the ATC service claim.

cards.questionEn: What factors would you consider if you encountered heavy rain during approach?
cards.questionZh: 进近过程中遇到大雨时，你会考虑哪些因素？
cards.answerEn: I would consider the reduced visibility, engine performance, runway condition, and reported braking action. I would also assess the risk of a runway overrun on a wet surface. If I did not have the required visual reference at the minimum, I would go around.

selectedSources.sourceQuestionEn: If you encounter heavy rain during approach what factors will you consider?
selectedSources.text: If there is heavy rain during approach, we will consider low visibility, engine performance, runway condition, and braking action. If no contact at minimum due to heavy rain, we will go around. What's more, if the runway surface is wet, we may overrun the runway.

editActions: organized visibility, engine, runway, braking, and minima factors
kept the go-around decision
cards.riskAssessment: Every factor and decision is explicit in v1.

cards.questionEn: Have you ever flown in heavy rain?
cards.questionZh: 你曾在大雨中飞行过吗？
cards.answerEn: Yes, I have flown through heavy rain during an approach. I used the windshield wipers, monitored visibility and runway braking action, and adjusted the approach speed in accordance with the procedure. Although visibility was reduced and the landing distance increased, I maintained a stable approach and landed safely.

selectedSources.sourceQuestionEn: Have you ever flown in heavy rain?
selectedSources.text: Yes, I’ve flown in heavy rain during approach to XX airport. I focused on visibility (windshield wipers on), monitored runway braking action, and adjusted approach speed. Heavy rain reduced visibility and increased landing distance, but I maintained stable flight and landed safely by following procedures.

editActions: removed the unresolved airport placeholder
kept the approach example, monitoring, procedural adjustment, and outcome
cards.riskAssessment: Every action and outcome is explicit in v1; the missing airport name was omitted.

cards.questionEn: How can heavy rain affect a flight?
cards.questionZh: 大雨会如何影响飞行？
cards.answerEn: Heavy rain can reduce visibility and obscure the windshield. It can reduce runway braking action and increase the risk of an overrun or runway excursion. It may also affect engine performance and aircraft stability during approach.

selectedSources.sourceQuestionEn: What are the bad influences if you fly in heavy rain?
selectedSources.text: Heavy rain reduces visibility, obscures windshields, and impairs braking action on runways, increasing the risk of overrun or veering off. It may also cause engine performance issues and affect aircraft stability during approach.

editActions: organized visibility, braking, engine, stability, and runway risks
repaired cohesion
cards.riskAssessment: Every effect is explicit in v1.

cards.taskTitle: 运行-旅客异常情况处置-1
cards.questionEn: How should a flight crew respond when passengers become anxious during a long delay?
cards.questionZh: 长时间延误导致乘客焦虑时，机组应如何应对？
cards.answerEn: The flight crew should explain the reason for the delay in a clear passenger announcement and continue to provide updated information. The cabin crew can offer food and drinks when available and speak calmly with anxious passengers.

selectedSources.sourceQuestionEn: get anxious during long delay
selectedSources.text: First of all, I will make a PA to explain the reason for delay/diversion. Secondly, I will ask cabin crew to provide some food and drinks. At last, I will keep informing the PAX of the latest flight information.

editActions: kept explanation, basic service, and continuing updates
made the response directly address passenger anxiety
cards.riskAssessment: Every response is explicit in v1.

cards.taskTitle: 运行-旅客异常情况处置-2
cards.questionEn: How should a flight crew respond when passengers complain about a diversion?
cards.questionZh: 乘客抱怨备降时，机组应如何应对？
cards.answerEn: The crew should explain the reason for the diversion calmly and make clear that the decision was taken for safety. Passengers should receive timely updates, and the cabin crew can answer questions and provide basic services such as food or drinks when available.

selectedSources.sourceQuestionEn: complain about the diversion
selectedSources.text: First of all, I will make a PA to explain the reason for delay/diversion. Secondly, I will ask cabin crew to provide some food and drinks. At last, I will keep informing the PAX of the latest flight information.

selectedSources.sourceQuestionEn: If some passengers complain about the diversion, what should you do as a captain?
selectedSources.text: As captain, I will ask cabin crew to explain the reason (for example safety concerns) patiently, provide timely updates, offer basic services (food/drinks), and emphasize that diversion prioritizes their safety. Maintain calm communication to ease anxiety.

editActions: combined diversion explanation, safety rationale, updates, calm communication, and basic services
removed repetitive statements
cards.riskAssessment: Every response is explicit in v1.

cards.taskTitle: 运行-旅客异常情况处置-3
cards.questionEn: What should a flight crew do if a passenger becomes ill or feels unwell during flight?
cards.questionZh: 飞行中乘客生病或感觉不适时，机组应如何处置？
cards.answerEn: The flight crew should ask the cabin crew to provide first aid and monitor the passenger. They should inform ATC, and if the passenger's condition requires it, divert to a suitable airport and request medical assistance on arrival.

selectedSources.sourceQuestionEn: PAX get ill feel uncomfortable/suffer from heart attack/get injured during turbulence
selectedSources.text: First of all, I will ask the cabin crew to give them first aid and take good care of him. Secondly, I will advise ATC of our situation, if necessary, I will request divert to the nearest suitable airport and medical assistance.

editActions: kept cabin first aid, care, ATC notification, conditional diversion, and medical assistance
repaired pronouns and grammar
cards.riskAssessment: Every response is explicit in v1 and diversion is correctly conditional.

cards.taskTitle: 运行-旅客异常情况处置-4
cards.questionEn: What should a flight crew do if a drunk or unruly passenger disrupts a flight?
cards.questionZh: 醉酒或行为不当的乘客干扰飞行时，机组应如何处置？
cards.answerEn: The captain should ask the cabin crew and, if one is on board, the air marshal to de-escalate the situation, separate the passenger from others, and maintain cabin order. If the passenger remains dangerous, an air marshal who is present may restrain and monitor the person. If the situation cannot be controlled, the crew should inform ATC and arrange airport security assistance on arrival.

selectedSources.sourceQuestionEn: If there is a drunken passenger quarreling with one of the flight attendants in the cabin, what should you do as the captain?
selectedSources.text: If there’s a drunken passenger arguing with a flight attendant in the cabin, as the captain, I’d first instruct the purser and air marshal to respond. They should calmly de - escalate the situation, ensure the passenger is controlled without escalation, and maintain cabin order. If the situation remains unmanageable, I’d communicate with ATC to report the incident and coordinate with airport security for assistance upon arrival, prioritizing flight safety and passenger well - being throughout.

selectedSources.sourceQuestionEn: drunk(unruly) PAX on board in flight
selectedSources.text: I will ask the air marshal to keep him away from other PAX. If he is being unruly, I will let the air marshal restrain him and monitor him.

editActions: kept calm de-escalation, separation, monitoring, conditional restraint, ATC, and security coordination
removed automatic priority-landing wording
cards.riskAssessment: Every retained response is explicit in v1 and escalation is conditional.

cards.taskTitle: 运行-旅客异常情况处置-5
cards.questionEn: What should a flight crew do if passengers start fighting on board?
cards.questionZh: 机上乘客开始打架时，机组应如何处置？
cards.answerEn: The flight crew should ask the cabin crew to speak to the passengers and stop the fight. If they continue and cannot be controlled, an air marshal who is on board may restrain them. Airport police should be requested to deal with the passengers after landing.

selectedSources.sourceQuestionEn: fight between the PAX
selectedSources.text: I will ask the cabin crew to communicate with them to stop the fight. If they don't listen and keep fighting, I will ask the air marshal to restrain them. After landing, I will request the airport police to take them away.

editActions: kept verbal intervention, conditional restraint, and police handover
repaired cohesion
cards.riskAssessment: Every response is explicit in v1.

cards.taskTitle: 运行-旅客异常情况处置-6
cards.questionEn: What should a flight crew do if passengers are injured by turbulence?
cards.questionZh: 如果乘客因颠簸受伤，机组应如何处置？
cards.answerEn: The pilots should maintain stable flight while the cabin crew provides first aid and asks whether a doctor is on board. The crew should inform ATC of the injuries. If necessary, they should request priority landing and arrange for an ambulance on arrival.

selectedSources.sourceQuestionEn: What would you do if you have passengers injured due to turbulence?
selectedSources.text: First, I maintain stable flight control. Then, I ask cabin crew to provide first aid and find a doctor on board. I inform ATC of the situation, request priority landing and ambulance at the destination, ensuring the injured passenger gets timely medical treatment.

selectedSources.sourceQuestionEn: What would you do if you have passengers injured due to turbulence?
selectedSources.text: If passengers are injured during turbulence, I first maintain stable flight control. I instruct the cabin crew to provide first aid and find a doctor on board if possible. I then inform ATC of the situation, request priority landing, and arrange for an ambulance to be available upon arrival to ensure timely medical treatment.

editActions: combined aircraft control, first aid, doctor search, ATC, landing, and ambulance actions
made the landing response condition-dependent
cards.riskAssessment: Every response is explicit in v1 and landing priority is conditional.

cards.taskTitle: 运行-旅客异常情况处置-7
cards.questionEn: What should a flight crew do if a passenger has a heart attack during flight?
cards.questionZh: 飞行中如果乘客突发心脏病，机组应如何处置？
cards.answerEn: The flight crew should ask the cabin crew to provide first aid and make an announcement to find a doctor on board. They should inform ATC, land at a suitable airport, and request medical assistance on arrival.

selectedSources.sourceQuestionEn: If one passenger suffered from heart attack during flight, what would you do?
selectedSources.text: If one passenger suffered from heart attack, first, we will ask the flight attendants to offer first aid to him. Second, we will make a PA to find a doctor on board. Third, we will report our situation to ATC and request land at nearest suitable airport and medical services.

editActions: kept first aid, doctor search, ATC, landing, and medical assistance
repaired grammar
cards.riskAssessment: Every response is explicit in v1.

cards.taskTitle: 运行-旅客异常情况处置-8
cards.questionEn: What should you do if a passenger refuses to check oversized baggage at the gate?
cards.questionZh: 如果乘客在登机口拒绝托运超大行李，你应如何处理？
cards.answerEn: I would ask the purser to explain why the oversized baggage cannot be carried in the cabin and how it could injure people or affect flight safety. If the passenger still refused to comply, the captain could refuse boarding.

selectedSources.sourceQuestionEn: refuse to check his oversized baggage/turn off his mobile
selectedSources.text: We will tell him that checking the baggage/turning off his mobile is for flight safety. If he keeps refusing to check his oversized baggage/turn off his mobile, I will force him to check the baggage/turn off his mobile phone. As a captain, I can refuse him boarding.

selectedSources.sourceQuestionEn: If the passenger refuses to check in over-sized baggage at the gate, what will you do?
selectedSources.text: If the passenger refuses to check in over - sized baggage at the gate, I will ask the purser to deal with it. We can inform the passenger of the dangers of carrying the over - sized baggage into the cabin. For example, we can tell the passenger that over - sized baggage may cause damage to the aircraft or injury to persons on board, and it may affect flight safety.

editActions: kept purser involvement, safety explanation, and boarding refusal
removed coercive force wording
cards.riskAssessment: Every retained response is explicit in v1; coercive language was excluded.

cards.taskTitle: 运行-旅客异常情况处置-9
cards.questionEn: What should you do if a passenger refuses to turn off a mobile phone when instructed?
cards.questionZh: 如果乘客经要求后仍拒绝关闭手机，你应如何处理？
cards.answerEn: The cabin crew or purser should explain that the instruction is related to flight safety and ask the passenger to comply. If the passenger continues to refuse and disrupts the operation, the crew can involve the air marshal and arrange for airport security to handle the matter.

selectedSources.sourceQuestionEn: If the passenger refuses to turn off the cell phone, what will you do?
selectedSources.text: If the passenger refuses to turn off the cell phone, the flight attendants or the purser may inform the passenger that it may affect flight safety. For example, the passenger will be informed that it may interfere with the radio communication between the pilots and air traffic controllers.

selectedSources.sourceQuestionEn: If the passenger refuses to turn off the cell phone, what will you do?
selectedSources.text: Normally, this is handled by cabin crew and air marshals. I will instruct the cabin crew to explain the safety risks of mobile phone interference with aircraft systems. If the passenger persists and disturbs flight safety, contact airport security to handle it upon arrival and ensure no disruption to flight operations.

editActions: kept cabin-crew handling, safety explanation, continued-disruption condition, and security support
removed the specific radio-interference claim
cards.riskAssessment: Every retained response is explicit in v1; the over-specific interference explanation was excluded.

cards.questionEn: What medical assistance can cabin crew provide during a flight?
cards.questionZh: 飞行中，客舱机组可以提供哪些医疗救助？
cards.answerEn: Cabin crew can provide basic first aid, including bleeding control and bandaging, and can perform CPR in a cardiac arrest. They can use the onboard emergency medical kit under professional guidance, monitor the passenger, and keep the pilots informed.

selectedSources.sourceQuestionEn: What kind of medical help the cabin crew can provide during the flight?
selectedSources.text: For example, if the PAX is ill or gets injured, the cabin crew can give them first aid. If the PAX loses consciousness or suffers from a heart attack, the cabin crew can give them CPR.

selectedSources.sourceQuestionEn: What kind of medical help the cabin crew can provide during the flight?
selectedSources.text: Cabin crew can offer basic first aid, such as bleeding control, bandaging and CPR for cardiac arrest. They use on-board emergency medical kits under professional guidance. They monitor sick passengers, maintain cabin order and inform pilots. For serious emergencies, they assist in diverting and coordinating with ground medical services to ensure passengers receive timely treatment.

editActions: kept basic first aid, bleeding control, bandaging, CPR, medical kits, monitoring, and pilot notification
qualified professional guidance
cards.riskAssessment: Every form of assistance is explicit in v1.

cards.questionEn: Under what circumstances should a pilot declare a medical emergency?
cards.questionZh: 飞行员应在什么情况下宣布医疗紧急情况？
cards.answerEn: A pilot should declare a medical emergency when a crew member or passenger has a life-threatening condition or needs immediate medical assistance on the ground. Examples include pilot incapacitation, a heart attack, unconsciousness, severe injury, or uncontrollable bleeding. A critical assessment by a medical professional on board would also support the declaration.

selectedSources.sourceQuestionEn: Under what circumstances do you declare medical emergency?
selectedSources.text: There are many conditions/situations in which we will declare medical emergency. First, if the pilot gets incapacitated, we will declare medical emergency. Second, if the passenger gets seriously ill such as heart attack, we will declare medical emergency. Third, if the passengers get seriously injured, we will declare medical emergency.

selectedSources.sourceQuestionEn: Under what circumstances do you declare medical emergency?
selectedSources.text: I declare medical emergency when crew or passengers face life-threatening situations, such as severe injuries, heart attacks, unconsciousness, or uncontrollable bleeding. It’s also required if a medical professional on board confirms the situation is critical, needing immediate ground medical assistance.

editActions: combined life threat, incapacitation, serious illness, injury, unconsciousness, bleeding, and medical assessment
removed repetitive examples
cards.riskAssessment: Every threshold and example is explicit in v1.

cards.questionEn: How should first aid be provided to someone on board an aircraft?
cards.questionZh: 应如何为飞机上的人员提供急救？

consideredSources.sourceQuestionEn: How do you carry out first-aid to persons on board?
consideredSources.text: If the person on board needs first aid, the flight attendants can offer him or her oxygen supply. Then we will make a PA to find a doctor on board. Finally, we will report our situation to ATC and request land at nearest suitable airport and medical services.

editActions: rejected a universal oxygen instruction and the absence of any assessment or condition-appropriate first-aid process

cards.questionEn: Do you select an alternate airport for every flight? Why or why not?
cards.questionZh: 你是否为每次飞行都选择备降机场？为什么？
cards.answerEn: No, not for every flight. I do not plan an alternate for traffic-circuit training, but for cross-country training I plan suitable departure, en-route, and destination alternates.

selectedSources.sourceQuestionEn: Do you have any alternate airport planned for each flight?
selectedSources.text: 1）Yes, we have. When we fly traffic circuit, we don't plan an alternate airport. When we take cross - country training, we will plan the departure alternate airport, the en - route alternate airport and the destination alternate airport.

editActions: selected the source that distinguishes traffic-circuit and cross-country training
removed the conflicting every-flight and jurisdiction-specific claims
cards.riskAssessment: The distinction is explicit in v1; conflicting universal claims were excluded.

cards.questionEn: What circumstances may cause a flight to divert?
cards.questionZh: 哪些情况可能导致航班备降？
cards.answerEn: A flight may divert because of an aircraft problem such as a system failure, structural damage, fire, or depressurization. Medical emergencies, bomb threats, or hijacking may also require a diversion. Other causes include bad weather, low visibility, or restrictions at the destination.

selectedSources.sourceQuestionEn:
What are some possible reasons for diversion?
What may be the possible cause of diversion?
selectedSources.text: There are some reasons for diversion. For example, mechanical failure, aircraft system failure, adverse weather, passenger illness and so on.

selectedSources.sourceQuestionEn:
What are some possible reasons for diversion?
What may be the possible cause of diversion?
selectedSources.text: Diversion reasons include aircraft issues (system failure, structural damage, fire, depressurization), crew/passenger problems (medical emergency, bomb threat, hijack), and destination issues (bad weather, military activities, low visibility).

editActions: grouped aircraft, medical, security, weather, and destination causes

cards.riskAssessment: Every circumstance is explicit in v1.

cards.questionEn: Who should the flight crew coordinate with during a diversion?
cards.questionZh: 备降过程中，飞行机组应与哪些人员或单位协调？
cards.answerEn: During a diversion, the pilots should first coordinate within the flight crew. They should then contact ATC for clearance and guidance, keep the company dispatcher informed, and coordinate the revised plan with the alternate airport.

selectedSources.sourceQuestionEn: Who do you need to contact in case of diversion?
selectedSources.text: In case of diversion, I need to contact my company and then contact ATC.

selectedSources.sourceQuestionEn: Who do you need to contact in case of diversion?
selectedSources.text: I will first inform the flight crew, then contact ATC to report the situation and request clearance/guidance. I will also communicate with the company dispatcher to update the flight plan and coordinate with the alternate airport.

cards.riskAssessment: Every coordination party and purpose is explicit in v1.

cards.questionEn: Have you ever experienced a diversion? If so, what happened?
cards.questionZh: 你是否曾经历过备降？如果有，当时发生了什么？
cards.answerEn: No, I have never experienced a diversion.

selectedSources.sourceQuestionEn: Have you ever had any experience with diversion? If yes, please describe it.
selectedSources.text: No, I have never experienced diversion.

editActions: selected the complete negative example
rejected the alternate example with unresolved route and airport placeholders

cards.questionEn: What factors should a flight crew consider when selecting a diversion airport?
cards.questionZh: 选择备降机场时，飞行机组应考虑哪些因素？
cards.answerEn: The crew should consider the weather, fuel endurance, runway length and condition, and the airport's available facilities. Ground handling, fire and medical services, and maintenance support may also affect the choice.

selectedSources.sourceQuestionEn: What information do you need to know about your alternate airport before diversion?
selectedSources.text: Before diversion, I need to know a lot of information about the alternate airport such as the weather at the alternate airport, the facilities and assistance the alternate airport can provide, the runway length and runway condition and so on.

selectedSources.sourceQuestionEn: What considerations will you have when choosing an alternate airport?
selectedSources.text: There are many factors we will consider when choosing the alternate airport, such as the weather information and runway conditions of the alternate airport, fuel endurance, ground services and so on.

selectedSources.sourceQuestionEn: Suppose you want to divert to the nearest airport due mechanic problem and there are two airports in the vicinity, which one do you prefer to Choose, a bigger, international airport or a smaller airport?
selectedSources.text: I will choose the bigger international airport. It has better emergency services (fire/medical), longer runways, more maintenance support, and sufficient ground facilities—critical for handling mechanical issues and ensuring safe landing/evacuation if needed.

editActions: combined weather, fuel, runway, ground, emergency, and maintenance factors
removed the automatic preference for a large international airport
cards.riskAssessment: Every selection factor is explicit in v1.

selectedSources.sourceQuestionEn: What is unlawful interference in civil aviation? Can you give some examples?
selectedSources.text: Unlawful interference means any act that threatens the safety of civil aviation. Examples include hijacking, bomb threats, sabotage of aircraft or airport facilities, taking hostages on board, and using an aircraft as a weapon.
